gate_statement: The Candidate Governance Review Gate MUST remain NO-GO from code-review scope. Absence of a STAGED_EXACT proof is normal for Candidate Review and is not itself a blocker; the blockers are that the candidate can later accept forged scope, waiver, authority and staged-proof claims as valid or GO.

findings.title: Intent and Classification scope do not constrain Blueprint or change-scope writes
findings.evidence: validatePhaseScope checks the Blueprint write paths against only the Phase policy, and assignment writes against only Phase plus Blueprint. It never requires Blueprint or assignment writes to be within task-intent.scope.include or classification.scope.include. validate-change-scope then uses the already-wider Blueprint or assignment paths as its authority.

reproduction.method: Read-only in-memory calls to the production exports
reproduction.command_summary: Call validatePhaseScope with Intent and Classification limited to .codex/tasks/APPROVED/** while Blueprint and documentation-engineer assignment allow .codex/tasks/UNAPPROVED/**; then call validateChangedPaths for product/.codex/tasks/UNAPPROVED/file.md.

findings.impact: A structurally valid Task can bypass the human-approved Intent and Classification scope while remaining under the broad Phase and role roots. The deterministic change-scope gate accepts the unauthorized path, so a scope-approval boundary can be bypassed without hardcoding a product directory.
findings.required_resolution: Compute one effective read/write intersection across Phase policy, Intent, Classification, Blueprint, role policy and assignment, and make validate-change-scope consume only that computed intersection. Add an integration fixture that expects rejection for a Phase-allowed but Intent/Classification-disallowed path.

findings.title: Forged candidate and staged proof fields plus generic PASS evidence still produce GO
findings.evidence: The main validator does not import or call validateCandidateBinding or validate-staged-candidate. It accepts any PASS check or artifact for scope_validation and preapproval_gate, checks only WORKSPACE_CANDIDATE/STAGED_EXACT labels plus change_scope_result, and merely requires the two evidence_ref strings to differ. The helper itself ignores candidate included_file_set_sha256 and staged file/blob set hashes. The built-in complete-GO fixture supplies constant A/B/C hashes, file_count 1, and generic EV-SCOPE/EV-PREAPP checks even though the copied governance manifest is the 103-file candidate; CASE-01 explicitly expects validateTask to return GO.

reproduction.method: Read-only source inspection plus in-memory production-helper call
reproduction.command_summary: Call validateCandidateBinding with the expected manifest hash/count but deliberately wrong candidate included-file-set hash and staged file/blob-set hashes.
reproduction.observed: candidate_binding_errors=[]; the manifest-covered fixture contract also defines the same class of forged proof as CASE-01 expected GO.

findings.impact: Final commit approval can be forged without a proof produced by the actual staged-candidate validator, without exact file/blob binding, and without genuine scope or preapproval executions. This is an in-contract incorrect GO and wrong-binding path.
findings.required_resolution: Integrate schema-validated, hash-bound proof artifacts into validateTask; bind manifest hash, candidate path+content set, staged path set, staged blob set, file count, task ID, execution ID and execution time; require scope and preapproval evidence types produced by their designated validators, not generic PASS records. Add an integration fixture where every fake field is rejected.

findings.title: Human waiver validation is not integrated and duplicate requirement IDs can downgrade non-waivable semantics
findings.evidence: validateWaiver exists only as a helper and contract-fixture target; validateTask neither imports it nor resolves, schema-validates, hashes or authority-checks waiver_artifact_id. A non-waivable check can also be paired with two different requirement objects sharing one requirement_id because schema uniqueItems applies to whole objects. requirementById is a Map built from the array, so the last duplicate silently becomes authoritative.

reproduction.method: Read-only schema validation and Map selection using production validateSchema
reproduction.command_summary: Validate test evidence containing REQ-ONE first as EVIDENCE_INTEGRITY/waiver_allowed=false and again as GENERAL/waiver_allowed=true, then a NOT_APPLICABLE check referencing waiver_artifact_id=FAKE.
reproduction.observed: schema_issues=[] and Map selected the later GENERAL/waiver_allowed=true record. A separate call showed validateWaiver would reject an agent-produced, empty-control, late waiver, proving the protection exists but is not in the authoritative path.

findings.impact: An opaque L3 integrity requirement can be semantically downgraded and waived by a nonexistent, late or agent-authored artifact. Since NOT_APPLICABLE is allowed by the final required-evidence check, this can remove a required gate control and permit incorrect GO.
findings.required_resolution: Reject duplicate requirement_id values before Map construction; derive non-waivability from the unique semantic record and classification; resolve the referenced waiver artifact uniquely; validate its schema, hash, producer, approver authority, requirement/category/task binding, scope approval, alternative control and chronology in validateTask.

findings.title: Global Domain approval lookup still uses first-match authority within each manifest
findings.evidence: findManifestArtifacts uses Array.find, so it records at most one matching artifact per task manifest. The later artifacts.length===1 check therefore means one matching task manifest, not one matching artifact record. validateArtifactIdentities protects only the currently validated Task manifest; global authority lookup does not validate every searched manifest. The Remediation 4 fixtures exercise only the isolated helper and do not exercise this global first-match path.

reproduction.command_summary: Place two different artifact records with one approval artifact ID in a searched task manifest; Array.find returns the first and findManifestArtifacts pushes one match, so artifacts.length is 1.
reproduction.observed: The second conflicting artifact is invisible to the global uniqueness decision.

findings.impact: A conflicting or forged Domain approval identity can be hidden behind the first record and accepted as globally unique authority, violating the no-first-match authority contract.
findings.required_resolution: Collect all matching artifacts from every manifest, reject any duplicate before authority lookup, and validate the identity field set for every searched manifest. Add a production-path integration fixture with two same-ID records in one non-current manifest.

findings.title: Chronology is enforced, but not-required sensitivity is derived from only free-form trigger text
findings.evidence: The ordered-stage calculation now includes both approved and not-required decisions and requires the execution decision before implementation start. However, sensitiveExecution is a regex over classification.triggers only. The schema and validator do not derive or cross-check sensitivity from Intent, classification reasons/scope, Blueprint execution/scope, evidence categories or external-reference content.
findings.impact: A sensitive Task whose trigger list omits the magic words can use not-required execution approval. The chronology is correct for the supplied classification, but the classification-to-decision derivation remains fail-open.
findings.required_resolution: Use structured execution categories and semantic evidence categories to derive sensitivity, cross-check them across Intent, Classification and Blueprint, and add approved/not-required chronology fixtures for both legitimate and omitted-category cases.

findings.title: The exact 50-case parent report contract is sound, but the 54-case suite gives false assurance about production integration
findings.evidence: The parent validator rejects truncated, duplicate, missing, unexpected, malformed-hash, wrong-version and wrong-case-manifest reports; read-only adversarial probes returned nonzero errors for all six classes, and the recorded case-manifest hash equals the canonical hash of the exact 50 IDs. But the 54-case suite mostly calls helpers that the authoritative validator does not call. Its chronology cases R4-18 through R4-20 are tautological integer comparisons rather than production checks, and the suite emits only lines plus a count summary rather than a versioned exact-set report. Therefore 54/54 can coexist with the incorrect GO paths above.
findings.impact: A green 54/54 report is a false claim of integrated remediation coverage and cannot support Candidate Gate passage.
findings.required_resolution: Convert helper checks into end-to-end validateTask/change-scope fixtures, replace tautologies with production calls, and give the 54-case suite its own versioned exact case manifest, structured report and parent-side exact-set/hash validation.

conditions.condition: Resolve A4-CODE-BLOCKER-001 through A4-CODE-BLOCKER-004 and independently rerun an exact candidate-bound review.
Close the structured sensitivity derivation and integrated fixture coverage gaps before any governance commit preparation or execution decision.

decisions_required.decision: Keep the Candidate Governance Review Gate, Governance Commit Preparation Gate and Governance Commit Execution Gate at NO-GO; authorize remediation only if desired, followed by a fresh independent review of a new immutable candidate.
Keep the separate Migration 320 Gate at NO-GO. This review authorizes no product, database, migration, staging, commit, merge, push or release action.

fixture_execution.reason: Those runners create and delete .codex/tests/.tmp workspaces. The reviewer authorization allowed only code-review.json to be written. Filed fixture claims were inspected but not trusted as a substitute for production-path review.

residual_risks: Agent path policy is not OS or container isolation.
Reviewer and human identity assurance remains procedural rather than cryptographic.
The scanner is bounded deterministic pattern detection, not full DLP or proof of global sensitive-data absence.
Remote branch protection, CI/CODEOWNERS and repository-global branch/worktree restrictions were not verified.
Complete TOCTOU and filesystem reparse protection is outside this review.
Controlled evidence storage and actual staged state were not reviewed; no staged proof is expected at Candidate Review.
